title: First Man: The Life of Neil A. Armstrong
author: James R. Hansen
target_audience: Readers interested in space exploration and NASA history
Fans of biographies of extraordinary individuals
Students and educators in science and engineering
General readers intrigued by the Apollo program and American history
core_themes: The personal and professional journey of Neil Armstrong
The history of space exploration and the Apollo program
The tension between public heroism and private modesty
primary_purpose: To offer a comprehensive, authoritative, and nuanced portrait of Neil Armstrong—his life, his character, his achievements, and his place in history as the first human to walk on the Moon.

structure_format.narrative_style: Meticulously researched, detailed, and balanced; combining narrative biography with technical exposition
structure_format.organization: Chronological; from Armstrong's childhood through his career as an astronaut and life after Apollo 11
features: Extensive interviews with Armstrong, family, and colleagues
Archival research and use of primary sources
Technical explanations of engineering and flight
Analysis of Armstrong’s public and private life

key_concepts_lessons: Pioneering achievements require a blend of skill, discipline, and humility.
Armstrong’s technical expertise, calm under pressure, and commitment contributed to mission success.
Public myth and media narratives often contrast with the complex reality of iconic individuals.
Personal sacrifice and family impact play significant roles in great accomplishments.
Space exploration is not just a technological feat, but a deeply human endeavor.
notable_features: Only authorized biography of Neil Armstrong
Draws on hours of exclusive interviews with Armstrong
Detailed depiction of NASA operations and training
Balanced exploration of Armstrong’s personal and professional sides
cultural_historical_context: Published nearly 40 years after the Apollo 11 moon landing, the book offered new insight into Armstrong’s reclusive nature, at a time of renewed interest in space exploration and historical reflection on the Space Race era.
reception_impact: Critically acclaimed for depth of research and narrative clarity
Praised for humanizing Armstrong and filling gaps in public understanding
Became the definitive biography referenced in scholarship and media
Helped inspire broader public and cinematic interest in the Apollo era
Some readers noted the technical details could be challenging for general audiences
comparable_titles: Carrying the Fire by Michael Collins
Moon Shot by Alan Shepard and Deke Slayton
